utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor, it is the document that discusses war booty. Were vehicles from the TAS factory considered war booty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I expected you to put any question triggered by my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no. The questions I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's your witness cross-examined by --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you re-examined the witness extensively, and I think the war booty then in the final round was perhaps dealt with by Mr. Traldi, but you're now entering in a third round which is not the common thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I will refrain. I don't want to open a new practice. I was probably miscalculating my turn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah. It was short and I think we can deal even with these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And of course you ask these to be on the screen; of course. We'll critically read what kind of motor vehicle it was and et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll carefully consider the document, but I think there is no --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I apologise for this confusion. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is no compelling reason for a third round. This then concludes your evidence, Professor Lukic. I would like to thank you very much for having come a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, sometimes even more than that, questions put to you by the parties, questions put to you by the Bench. I wish to you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the parties will soon come up with the -- with any remaining associated exhibits. But the Chamber would prefer not to deal with them at this very moment because that would enhance the chances that the next witness could conclude his testimony before the weekend even before 2.00 today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hopefully he will. We can have only 15 minutes break, and I can tell you that I don't have any additional questions to him. I'm just read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No additional questions. So just cross-examination which was estimated at 30 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We expect cross-examination to be quite short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then it -- yes. Then we'll take a break. But not, Mr. Traldi, after I've heard what you would like to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just if we could mark for identification the last document used with the witness, 65 ter 02395, the assembly session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6742 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it keeps that status for the time being. Now, before we take the break I also have another small item on my agenda but which we'd have to deal with in private session. So for the audience, we'll be in private session for not more than one or two minutes. We'll then return in open session and take a break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and will resume at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the next witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see both Mr. Jeremy and Mr. McCloskey present. Mr. Jeremy, it will be you who will cross-examine the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Marjanovic, I take it. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Marjanovic, you will first be examined by, although it will be pretty short, if I understand Mr. Lukic well. You'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Marjanovic.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, please tell us your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Djordje Marjanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only it's without -- yes. Without "I." Can we have 1D1723 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you want to have the statement of the witness on the screen, the 92 ter motion was filed confidential --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It shouldn't be broadcasted, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shouldn't be broadcasted. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But basically it's only because second page, and I think that Mr. Jeremy already told me that he is not going to need that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say the cover page and the last page there will -- but if the -- if it's filed confidentially, then all the attachments are confidential automatically and we should strictly adhere to that in court as well, unless at any point in time you will file a different version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm fine with the -- proceeding this way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marjanovic, do you see your statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you indeed at some point provide a statement to General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see your signature on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Given the fact that in the transcript we only have your answer record as "I do," whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the last page of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it on this page?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I see it. It is my signature on this statement that contains nine pages, and the date is the 30th of June 2014.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The details you provided to us, are they truthful and accurate as recorded in the statement?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The details and the gist of the statement is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I put the same questions to you today, would you, in principle, provide the same answers as you did when you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my answers would remain the same and the gist of the statement would as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just tender this statement into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D640 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D640 under seal admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, since there are portions of this statement which apparently are of concern as far as the public character is concerned, for the parties, Mr. Jeremy knows, apparently, what the sensitive issues are. I do not know. So if I would have any questions, I wouldn't know whether I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- Your Honour, it's just paragraph 3.

utterances.text: Paragraph 3. Only --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On second page, yes.

utterances.text: Yes. Only paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: That's clear to me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just, with your leave, Your Honour, read a short summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Djordje Marjanovic testifies about the situation in Sarajevo immediately before the war broke out. Djordje Marjanovic testifies about the lining up of Juka's unit and he depicts their uniforms and arms. He also claims that Juka's unit was funded through by the Tow Service. He remembers the killing of the Serb police officer in the police station Novo Sarajevo in early 1992. Juka's unit was involved in that killing. After the attack, barricades were set up around Sarajevo. After the setting up of barricades, Muslims intensified checking the citizens' IDs, which imposed the segregation of Serbs and limited their movements. Djordje Marjanovic testifies about the subordination of Juka's paramilitary units and the official units of the special police of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. In Han Pijesak, he joined the battalion of the military police of the protection regiment where he stayed until 23rd March 1993 when he became General Mladic's personal security guard. In September 1992, he was wounded in the operation in Zepa and he claims it was an action planned to destroy the General Staff of VRS. In his testimony, he speaks in detail about the general's humane and positive treatment of prisoners of war and non-Serb population. Djordje Marjanovic claims that the attempted assassination of General Mladic was done by sniper 12.7-millimetre, shot by a member of a French Battalion, on which occasion a cousin of Kenjic Mlado was killed. Marjnovic was not General Mladic's security guard during the Srebrenica July 1995 operation. He was on a 10-day leave and concluded that if there had been any plan for the Srebrenica July 1995 operation, he wouldn't have been granted leave. That was short summary and we do not have any questions for this witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only, I see, Mr. Marjnovic wants to tell something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Marjanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one minor correction. Mlado Kenjic was not killed. He was seriously wounded. And there was a cousin of his with him who is also related to General Mladic. I think his last name was Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that I read the cousin of Kenjic Mlado was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that the statement is the evidence and in the statement it says that he was seriously wounded. So therefore that is well understood. Mr. Marjanovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Jeremy. You'll find him to your right. Mr. Jeremy is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Marjanovic.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now I'd like to start by clarifying the dates that you left Sarajevo in 1992. Looking at paragraphs 18 to 21 of your statement, it appears you left on around the 10th of May 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date but it was in May when the JNA was withdrawing from the B and H. And then we went to Serbia, specifically from the Rajlovac barracks via Olovo, Bratunac. Half the unit went to Sombor and half of them went to the Zarkovo facility in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move now from Sarajevo and I'd like to go to your role in the close protection unit of General Mladic. Now, in the last sentence of paragraph 39 of your statement, referring to your period of leave during the Srebrenica events, you mention a person called Puhalo. Now, you're referring to Branislav Puhalo; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And he was your commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer. The interpreters couldn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My immediate superior from whom I received my orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now in July 1995, you accompanied General Mladic to the check-point at Boksanica just outside Zepa; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And it's also correct that you have previously seen footage of General Mladic boarding buses of civilians passing through this check-point at Boksanica; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure what you mean when you say footage. Actually, the question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'll try and be clearer. Do you recall an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in March 2012?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I had the interview in Banja Luka in the OHR offices. I remember that. I don't remember the exact date, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: During that interview, do you remember being shown some -- a video recording of yourself and General Mladic getting on and off buses at this check-point in Boksanica?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if they showed the video recording or not, but I know that the lady who was conducting the interview with me said that I was there in that footage and that I hadn't really changed sense. It's possible that there is that footage. And I explained to her then, and I can explain it to you, if necessary, why I was entering those buses, what the reason for that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll shortly get to that footage. I'll actually show you the clip. But before I do, it's the Prosecution's position that this event of the buses of civilians leaving or passing through the Boksanica check-point was on the 26th of July 1995. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but it was when it was. I mean, it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: But towards the end of July 1995. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: When the -- this occurred when the action around Zepa took place. That's when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And it was after the events in Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show you a portion of that footage now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we can just rely on what we see -- and would the transcript then be complete? Because the then the text does not appear on the transcript of this hearing.

utterances.text: It's already in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- where and how we've seen it before. utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.text: So if you would provide that as quickly as possible, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think that he commanded the Zvornik Brigade. Yes.

utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you a portion of General Mladic standing on the bus. Because of the instability of this recording, I think we'll go to a still of the portion that I want to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marjanovic, in paragraph 35 of your statement, you say that in 1993, you witnessed General Mladic say the following to refugees who were leaving Srebrenica. You state: "You said, he said, 'I am General Ratko Mladic. Some of you know me. Some don't. We did not need this. Do not join the army. I wish you a safe trip.'" Now, I understand that he said that to people who were leaving Srebrenica in 1993. In the next paragraph, paragraph 36, you state: "He would say the same at Zepa." Now, Mr. Marjanovic, having just seen the clip and having seen you standing next to General Mladic, it's clear that he said more than that at Zepa, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is footage from Zepa, not from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I understand. In paragraph 35, you're referring to Srebrenica and you refer to comments that Mladic made to refugees leaving Srebrenica. In paragraph 36, you say that he made the same comments to those persons leaving Zepa. And my question is very simply: It's clear that actually he said a fair bit more to those persons leaving Zepa; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't really know what you mean. He said what he said and that's been shown in the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you just let me try to ask you it in a different way. If you say that he said the same in Zepa as he said in Srebrenica, then he must have said more in Srebrenica than you quote because we hear what he says in Zepa, and if that's exactly the same as what he said in Srebrenica, then in Srebrenica he would have said more as well. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. As for Srebrenica, you could only see that from the media, from that footage. I wasn't in Srebrenica, so I really cannot speak about that. But I can speak about Zepa. That's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Do we then understand you well that what he said in Srebrenica, you have no direct knowledge of that, that you learned that from the media, and that what General Mladic may have said in Zepa, you know that because you were there and you heard it with your own ears? Is that how we have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- give the witness his statement, I think he's confusing 1993 and 1995. So if we clarify about this incident from 1993, whether he was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I leave that then to Mr. Jeremy. He started the comparison, to say so, and I just tried to clarify what you apparently wanted to ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And as far as I'm concerned, the statement is clear. I'm satisfied with the witness's answer to my question. I'd like to tender this -- this still, and otherwise I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the still would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6743, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6743 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there is nothing else --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I would have one question for you. In your statement in paragraph 38, you are referring to an attempted assassination of General Mladic. However, I do not see any point in time. Could you tell us when this was?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the precise time. I know it was summer. The man who was seriously wounded, Mladjen Tomic [phoen], he could give you the exact date because he was involved in the incident. I can tell you what I know about it if you need me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm mainly interested, first of all, on when it happened. Approximately you said it was in summer. Do you remember what year?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible that it was 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was before the Srebrenica events a year before that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you say the -- General Mladic was in Belgrade at the time. Your source of knowledge of that is what exactly? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was at our base. He left the base to go to Belgrade. That was the official information, that he had gone to Belgrade. We remained where we were. There was no need for us to go with him. And then there were two or -- one or two of his relative from the Belgrade, and I think they asked for transport to Vojkovici, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear to me you stayed at the base and General Mladic was reported to have left for Belgrade. Now, what is the basis for your knowledge on what happened in Lukavica? You say it was the members of the French Battalion of UNPROFOR that opened fire. How do you know that? You were not there, were you?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. I was given the option of going with the driver to escort them, but that it was not necessary. So they decided to go there by themselves. When the vehicle was near the Butmir airport, it was struck by sniper --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All I want to know is where you gained all that information.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: From the driver, Kenjic, who was wounded in that incident. After that General Mladic and I, a couple of days later, went to see him in hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That answers my question. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you -- if I may, Your Honour, I would just like to clarify potential confusion with paragraph 34 and 35. I would just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And my questions were only necessary, Mr. Lukic, because any time reference is missing. I've got no idea.

utterances.text: We couldn't --

utterances.text: Time reference is --

utterances.text: -- put time references to his mouth. We recorded what he remembers so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, about the assassination, the attempted assassination, there is no time reference whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll have Mr. Kenjic testifying here in the future. So I hope we will be able to clarify it with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 30, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go to paragraphs 34 and 35 in your statement.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: I have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you present in 1993 when the event you describe in paragraphs 34 and 35 happened?

utterances.text: Thank you. We have no further questions.
